note: The building config (D-89): archetype -> the declared art whose real footprint decides where it can stand. THIS IS THE EXTENSION POINT. Adding a building to the town is a data change — declare its art (contract + rects), add a row here, re-run scripts/derive-plots.mjs. No code moves. Footprints are DERIVED from contract/assets.contract.json maxSize (ceil to tiles), never written down here, so a prop that grows cannot silently keep a plot it no longer fits (D-79: physics constrains, and physics is read, not transcribed).

mobile_home.note: T1 of D-65's ladder. The smallest real dwelling the pack ships, and therefore the archetype that decides the smallest useful housing plot.

house.note: T2. The terraced house is the representative footprint; one_story_house and country_house are larger members of the same tier and are listed separately so a plot that fits only the smaller one says so.

house_detached.note: Same venue archetype as `house`, a bigger exterior. Kept a separate row because footprint fit is per-EXTERIOR, not per-venue: a plot may admit a terraced house and not a detached one.

condo.note: D-76: authored, dormant. condo_9 is the smallest of the three whole-building condos; condo_6 (13x16) needs an L plot.

museum.note: Composed facade (ground floor + middle floor + roof), so no single sprite carries its height. The footprint is authored from the composition the archetype describes: 112px wide, 48+64+96 = 208px tall.

swimming_pool.note: The pool is modular 16x16 water pieces plus deck furniture, not one sprite, so its footprint is an authored composition rather than a bitmap bound. 12x10 is the pool the archetype's furniture describes.

garden.note: Outdoor composition (D-75: no interior). The footprint is the archetype's own sizeTiles — venues/_archetypes/garden.json — because a park is the parcel, not a building on it.
